catalog.name: Groundwater & Water Storage
catalog.description: GRACE mission data showing changes in Earth's water storage including groundwater depletion, seasonal water cycles, and long-term hydrological trends. Essential for understanding regional water security and climate impacts on water resources.

info.name: Attribution
info.content: Data from NASA/DLR GRACE and GRACE Follow-On missions. Processing by NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL), Center for Space Research University of Texas (CSR), and GeoForschungsZentrum Potsdam (GFZ). Contact: earthdata-support@nasa.gov

info.name: License
info.content: NASA data is generally available for public use. Please cite GRACE mission and appropriate processing centers in publications.

info.name: Scientific Applications
info.content: Groundwater monitoring, drought assessment, seasonal water cycle analysis, ice mass balance, regional water security studies, climate change impacts on water resources.

members.name: GRACE Liquid Water Equivalent
members.description: Liquid Water Equivalent Thickness represents changes in total water storage (groundwater, soil moisture, surface water, snow, ice) measured by GRACE satellite gravimetry.

members.name: GRACE Liquid Water Equivalent (JPL Mascon)
members.description: Monthly water storage changes from GRACE JPL Mascon solution, providing high spatial resolution water storage variations with reduced leakage effects.

info.name: Background
info.content: The GRACE (Gravity Recovery and Climate Experiment) mission measures tiny changes in Earth's gravity field caused by mass redistribution, primarily water movement. The JPL Mascon solution uses a regularized least squares approach to reduce leakage and improve spatial resolution.

info.name: Measurement Principle
info.content: GRACE measures changes in Earth's gravity field by tracking distance changes between twin satellites. Water mass changes alter local gravity, allowing detection of groundwater depletion, seasonal water cycles, and ice loss.

info.name: Spatial Resolution
info.content: ~300 km effective spatial resolution, 0.5° × 0.5° grid spacing

info.name: Temporal Coverage
info.content: April 2002 - June 2017 (GRACE), June 2018 - present (GRACE Follow-On)

info.name: Measurement Units
info.content: Liquid Water Equivalent Thickness in centimeters (cm), representing equivalent height of water

info.name: JPL Mascon Advantages
info.content: Reduced leakage between regions, improved signal recovery, better representation of sharp boundaries like coastlines, enhanced spatial localization

info.name: Applications
info.content: Regional groundwater depletion studies, agricultural water management, drought monitoring, water security assessment, climate change impacts

info.name: Attribution
info.content: NASA GRACE/GRACE-FO missions, NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL), California Institute of Technology

members.name: GRACE Liquid Water Equivalent (CSR)
members.description: Monthly water storage changes from GRACE CSR (Center for Space Research) spherical harmonics solution, providing long-term consistent time series.

info.name: Background
info.content: The CSR solution uses traditional spherical harmonics approach to process GRACE gravity field data. It provides one of the longest consistent time series for climate studies and trend analysis.

info.name: Processing Approach
info.content: Spherical harmonics expansion up to degree/order 60, with standard filtering applied to reduce correlated errors

info.name: Strengths
info.content: Long consistent time series, well-validated for climate studies, standard processing approach allows for intercomparison with other solutions

info.name: Applications
info.content: Long-term trend analysis, climate change studies, seasonal cycle characterization, interannual variability assessment

info.name: Attribution
info.content: Center for Space Research, University of Texas at Austin, NASA GRACE/GRACE-FO missions

members.name: GRACE Liquid Water Equivalent (GFZ)
members.description: Monthly water storage changes from GRACE GFZ (GeoForschungsZentrum) solution, providing independent validation of water storage variations.

info.name: Background
info.content: The GFZ solution provides an independent analysis of GRACE gravity field data using different processing techniques, offering valuable comparison and validation for water storage studies.

info.name: Processing Center
info.content: GeoForschungsZentrum Potsdam (GFZ), Germany - one of the three official GRACE processing centers

info.name: Validation Value
info.content: Provides independent validation of water storage changes, helps assess uncertainty in GRACE-based water storage estimates

info.name: Applications
info.content: Uncertainty assessment, method comparison studies, robust trend detection through multi-solution analysis

info.name: Attribution
info.content: GeoForschungsZentrum Potsdam (GFZ), Germany, NASA/DLR GRACE/GRACE-FO missions

members.name: Regional Water Storage Analysis
members.description: Specialized GRACE products focusing on specific regions or domains for detailed water resource analysis.

members.name: GRACE Land Water Storage (Monthly)
members.description: Land-focused water storage changes from GRACE, isolating terrestrial water cycle variations from ocean mass changes.

info.name: Background
info.content: This product focuses specifically on land water storage changes, excluding ocean mass variations to provide clearer signals of terrestrial water cycle changes including groundwater, soil moisture, surface water, and snow.

info.name: Domain Focus
info.content: Continental landmasses only, excluding ocean areas for focused terrestrial water analysis

info.name: Key Features
info.content: Enhanced signal-to-noise over land areas, better representation of groundwater and surface water changes, reduced contamination from ocean signals

info.name: Applications
info.content: Terrestrial water balance studies, groundwater assessment, agricultural water monitoring, land surface model validation, drought characterization

info.name: Attribution
info.content: NASA GRACE/GRACE-FO missions, specialized land-focused processing

members.name: GRACE Water Storage Anomalies
members.description: Water storage anomalies relative to long-term mean, highlighting drought conditions, water surplus/deficit, and unusual hydrological events.

info.name: Background
info.content: Water storage anomalies represent deviations from the long-term average water storage, making it easier to identify drought conditions, wet periods, and long-term trends in water availability.

info.name: Reference Period
info.content: Anomalies calculated relative to 2004-2009 baseline period

info.name: Interpretation
info.content: Negative anomalies indicate below-normal water storage (drought conditions), positive anomalies indicate above-normal water storage (wet conditions)

info.name: Applications
info.content: Drought monitoring and early warning, water resource planning, climate impact assessment, extreme event detection, seasonal forecasting support

info.name: Attribution
info.content: NASA GRACE/GRACE-FO missions, anomaly processing by NASA Goddard Space Flight Center
